evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 女: glyph account and early usage
evidence.text: CUHK describes oracle-bone and bronze 女 as a kneeling woman, with knees and toes on the ground, seated on her heels and hands crossed at the chest; later bronze forms simplify the seated posture. It reports early graphic overlap/use of 女 for 母, 毋, 每/悔 and place names; bronze uses include female, mother, second-person 汝, and 如 ‘as’. These are reported uses, not stages in the graph’s shape history.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 女

evidence.source: 常用漢字二百字探源（金真姬）
evidence.field: 女 entry: glyph history and oracle-bone examples
evidence.text: The account reports oracle-bone and early bronze 女 as a side-view kneeling woman, with hands engaged in an activity, and says the original shape had become unrecognizable by the Warring States period. It cites oracle-bone examples in 合集14002正 for female, 殷虛文字綴合94 for a reading as 母, and other records involving female ancestors/consorts and a female person. These examples are cited by the book; their precise artifact dates were not individually verified here.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.source: 說文解字, quoted in CUHK Chinese Characters Database
evidence.text: The entry quotes Xu Shen: 女 means ‘woman’, is pictographic, and is the form used by graphs in the 女 series. This is a Han-period dictionary analysis, not direct evidence for the original Shang depiction.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 女

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 女: forms, graphic classification and meanings
evidence.text: The entry labels 女 pictographic and supplies oracle-bone and bronze forms. It lists senses including woman, daughter, to marry, and second-person pronoun, but does not provide a dated semantic sequence; the list alone does not establish when those senses arose.
evidence.title: 女(オンナ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.field: File description, depiction and reuse rights
evidence.text: The file page identifies 女-oracle.svg as a modern vector depiction of 女 in Shang oracle-script style, credits the glyph model to a Xiaoxuetang record labelled 43.EC6E, and associates it with 合3298. The page states CC0 1.0/public-domain reuse for the image. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph or scan of an ancient artifact.
evidence.kind: glyph image description and rights record
evidence.title: File:女-oracle.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: File description, depiction and reuse rights
evidence.text: The file page identifies 女-bronze.svg as a modern vector depiction of 女 in bronze-script style. It records sources including the Sinica database and Chinese Etymology, and states public-domain licensing for the SVG representation. The description does not identify a specific dated vessel for this drawing.
evidence.kind: glyph image description and rights record
evidence.title: File:女-bronze.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: 小學堂字形演變資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The official database homepage identifies the project as jointly developed by Academia Sinica’s Institute of History and Philology and Institute of Information Science, and reports its current scale. Its query interface was not successfully opened for an individual 女 form in this research.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變資料庫

evidence.text: The Taiwan Ministry of Education variant dictionary lists source collections for 女, including Shuowen Jiezi and references to paleographic collections. Its oracle-bone, bronze and other paleographic image fields shown on the opened page are marked unavailable to the public.
evidence.title: A00877 女 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Local supplied reading row; upstream Unicode record could not be inspected
evidence.text: The provided local primary row gives kMandarin 女 = nǚ. The official Unicode individual-record URL returned an internal error when opened, so the upstream record was not independently verified. This is modern reading metadata, not evidence for ancient graphic history.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan record for U+5973 女 (access attempt failed)

evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 女 ‘female’ MC nrjoX, OC *nraʔ and 女 ‘give as a wife’ MC nrjoH, OC *nraʔ-s. These are distinct lexical readings within that reconstruction system and do not establish the graph’s origin. No Baxter–Sagart phonetic component is proposed for 女 itself.
evidence.title: Local Baxter–Sagart table rows; no external click-through verified

gaps: No direct oracle-bone or bronze artifact photograph/rubbing was visually inspected. Proposed images are modern vector redrawings of ancient-script forms.

The Commons oracle drawing is linked to a Xiaoxuetang glyph label and an oracle-bone concordance number, but the exact individual Academia Sinica query record was not opened; use the Commons file provenance and rights statement for this candidate.
The Commons bronze drawing is not tied on its description page to a specific datable inscription; it illustrates a script style, not a dated specimen.

Accounts characterize hand position variously as hands crossed or hands engaged in an activity; explanations involving housework, submissiveness, or cultural symbolism are not secured by the graph alone.

CUHK and the cited paleographic dictionary report early graphical overlap/loan uses, but this search did not establish dated contextual attestations for 毋, 每/悔, 汝, 如 or place names. Those uses must remain distinct from graphic evolution.
No dated individual 女 inscription was verified here. The cited paleographic dictionary names corpus examples, but gives no secure date for those specific examples in the inspected passage.
No dated semantic chronology was established for daughter, marriage, feminine, or pronoun senses. Dictionary gloss lists do not demonstrate semantic transitions.
Unicode's exact Unihan page could not be inspected. The local kMandarin row is supplied evidence only. The locally supplied Baxter–Sagart rows likewise have no verified external click-through.
No other sound or semantic component applies: 女 is analyzed as an independent pictograph, not as a phono-semantic compound.

items.period: Shang oracle-bone script style; the file page associates the glyph model with oracle-bone record 合3298 but this redraw is not itself an artifact image
items.tradition: Modern vector redraw of an oracle-bone script form
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction of 女 in Shang oracle-bone style; paleographic accounts describe the early graph as a kneeling female figure.
items.alt: Black line drawing of an oracle-bone-style 女 form on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows the reported early pictographic form and is directly identified by its Commons description page, which supplies source attribution and CC0/public-domain reuse information.
items.rights: CC0 1.0/public domain as stated on the Commons file description page.

items.period: Bronze-script style; exact artifact date unspecified on file page
items.tradition: Modern vector redraw of a bronze-script form
items.caption: A modern vector drawing of 女 in bronze-script style; CUHK describes later bronze forms as simplifying the seated posture.
items.alt: Black line drawing of a bronze-script-style 女 form on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Offers a second script-style candidate relevant to the reported graphic simplification, with an inspected description and reuse statement; no claim that it is a photographed inscription.
items.rights: Public domain as stated for the SVG representation on the Commons file description page.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redrawings. The Commons pages provide script-style identification and reuse terms, but the research did not inspect their pixels or verify either against a particular artifact image.
The exact Xiaoxuetang query record for 女 and an official direct CC0 notice page were not successfully opened in this session; no Xiaoxuetang-rendered image is proposed.
